title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
description: Ten FSU spaces for quiet work, group projects, creative making, recreation, and time between classes, each supported by a direct university source.

cards.title: Match the Floor to the Assignment
cards.subtitle: Quiet floors and conversation-friendly zones in Strozier Library
cards.notes: Use floors 3–5 for quiet concentration; choose the first floor or designated parts of floor 2 when your group needs to talk.
cards.short_summary: A large library where students can deliberately choose between quiet and collaborative study settings.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries states that Strozier offers open-floor seating for hundreds, private study rooms, quiet areas in the basement and floors 2–5, and noise-permitted areas on floors 1–2.
cards.access_notes: Open study floors serve FSU students; private rooms have separate reservation or first-come, first-served rules.

cards.entity_name: Paul A. M. Dirac Science Library
cards.title: Switch Between Solo and Group Mode
cards.subtitle: Reservable rooms, group cubicles, and open floors at Dirac
cards.notes: Settle on floor 1 for quiet work, then move to floors 2–3 or reserve a group room when discussion becomes part of the task.
cards.short_summary: A science library with distinct noise zones and bookable spaces for individual or collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries identifies Dirac’s first floor as quiet, floors 2–3 as noise-permitted, and lists individual rooms, group rooms, and group cubicles available to students.
cards.access_notes: Room availability varies; consult the library booking system, while some listed spaces are first come, first served.

cards.title: Claim a Two-Hour Study Block
cards.subtitle: Open and reservable study space in the William Johnston Building
cards.notes: Use the first two floors for informal work, or reserve an individual or group room for a focused block of up to two hours.
cards.short_summary: An academic building whose lower floors and reservable rooms give students another study option beyond the libraries.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries says the first two floors of the William Johnston Building are open for studying and that individual and group rooms can be reserved in two-hour blocks.
cards.access_notes: The first two floors are open for study; rooms may be reserved up to two weeks ahead under current library rules.

cards.title: Study Beneath FSU’s Stained Glass
cards.subtitle: The Werkmeister Reading Room inside historic Dodd Hall
cards.notes: Bring reading work and pause to examine the windows and artifacts; confirm museum hours first because events and breaks can change access.
cards.short_summary: A historic reading room that combines study tables with exhibits documenting the university’s past.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Libraries locates the Heritage Museum in Dodd Hall’s Werkmeister Reading Room and says it displays university photographs, artifacts, and commemorative stained-glass windows.
cards.access_notes: Students and the public are encouraged to visit; check the Libraries hours page because breaks or events may alter access.

cards.title: Build a Between-Classes Base
cards.subtitle: Services, meeting spaces, recreation, and lounges under one roof
cards.notes: Check the building directory, then choose a lounge, meeting room, or recreation area that fits the time and purpose of your campus break.
cards.short_summary: A central multipurpose building where students can meet, handle errands, attend programs, or spend a break indoors.
cards.evidence_claim: The FSU Student Union says its building contains student services, meeting spaces, entertainment venues, lounges, bowling and billiards, and administrative offices.
cards.access_notes: Individual venues and meeting rooms may have separate schedules, eligibility requirements, reservations, or charges.

cards.title: Trade Screen Time for Shared Play
cards.subtitle: Cinema, gaming, and hands-on art at the ASLC
cards.notes: Look at the current program schedule, then meet friends for Student Life Cinema, the gaming lounge, or a Paint-A-Pot session.
cards.short_summary: A student-life venue grouping film, gaming, and creative activities in one identifiable campus destination.
cards.evidence_claim: The FSU Student Union identifies the Askew Student Life Center as a space for entertainment, recreation, and creativity, including Student Life Cinema, Garnet Gaming Lounge, and Paint-A-Pot.
cards.access_notes: Check each ASLC program or venue for its current schedule, admission policy, reservation rules, and possible activity fees.

cards.title: Turn a Group Idea Into a Prototype
cards.subtitle: Collaborative workspace and makerspace at 142 Collegiate Loop
cards.notes: Reserve a study room for planning, then ask Hub staff about the current process before using fabrication or immersive-media equipment.
cards.short_summary: A flexible campus workspace for studying, design collaboration, digital fabrication, and emerging-media projects.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU describes the Innovation Hub as an FSU-ID-accessible collaborative workspace and makerspace with study rooms, group space, a digital fabrication lab, and immersive-media resources.
cards.access_notes: Open to people with an FSU ID; study rooms are reservable, and equipment may require its own reservation or operating procedure.

cards.title: Find a Purpose-Built Pause
cards.subtitle: Student lounge, reflection room, and intercultural spaces
cards.notes: Use the lounge to meet, the reading room to slow down, or the meditation room for quiet reflection during its posted weekday access window.
cards.short_summary: A multicultural engagement building with several public student spaces designed for gathering, reading, and reflection.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s venue page says The Globe contains public student spaces including a lounge, Reflections Reading Room, café area, and a Meditation Room for the FSU community.
cards.access_notes: The cited page lists Meditation Room access from 8 a.m.–5 p.m.; other rooms and programs may have separate reservation rules.

cards.title: Gather, Recharge, or Compare Notes
cards.subtitle: Academic community space facing Landis Green
cards.notes: Use the house for peer study, a meeting, or a reset between commitments, while respecting any program-specific access and room rules.
cards.short_summary: A named academic-community building with gathering, study, meeting, and recharge spaces for participating students.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU’s Honors Program says the Honors, Scholars, and Fellows House contains spaces where students can study, socialize, meet with peers, or rest and recharge.
cards.access_notes: The building houses Honors and other academic-support programs; verify eligibility and reservations for particular rooms or services.

cards.title: Take Campus Life to Lake Bradford
cards.subtitle: Paddling, swimming, games, and shaded gathering space
cards.notes: Check facility status before leaving campus, pack closed-toe shoes if climbing, and follow staff directions around swimming and equipment checkout.
cards.short_summary: An off-main-campus FSU recreation site where students can paddle, swim, picnic, play field games, or gather in the shade.
cards.evidence_claim: FSU Campus Recreation describes the 73-acre Lake Bradford facility as offering kayaking, paddleboarding, swimming, disc golf, sand volleyball, a climbing wall, and picnic areas.
cards.access_notes: Four miles from main campus; check current hours and facility status. Admission, rentals, clinics, and guest access follow separate rules.
